Native source ownership and reconstructed text productions
==========================================================

Images are taken from data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. The extraction tool
uses the fixed native Windows objdump and PE unwind owners, never the running
game or a translation execution. native-owners.tsv records exact image identity,
path, literal address, instruction address and full owner bounds. The .asm files
retain complete owners, including every native branch/call. Printable immediate
bytes are operand evidence; numerically encoded unrelated data is not prose.

Mandate creation:
  reference 0x14134de20..0x14134eb2e
  classic   0x141348d90..0x141349a9e
  The native name/profession formatter is invoked with r8d=0.
  reference 0x14134e739 -> 0x141330c30
  classic   0x1413496a9 -> 0x14132bba0
  Mandate mode 1 appends " has mandated the construction of certain goods.".
  Mandate mode 0 appends " has imposed a ban on certain exports.".
  Price-change branch appends " has altered the prices of goods.".
  The same identity formatter precedes all three predicates. The identity is
  a typed unit reference, including profession/office and territorial title;
  it is not a whole-string personal name.

Demand changes:
  reference 0x14134ac10..0x14134bb1c
  classic   0x141345b80..0x141346a8c
  Old demand removal appends " has forgotten a demand.".
  New demand creation appends " has a new demand.".
  No separately authored success announcement occurs in these owners.

Mandate termination:
  reference 0x140e39910..0x140e3fde8
  classic   0x140e34880..0x140e3ad58
  Existing unit: unit formatter + " has ended a mandate.".
  Absent unit: "A mandate has ended.".
  The complete owner also constructs the missing-unit, Mountainhome royalty,
  and famine records. Their authored alternatives are handled as full messages
  in announcement-mandate-grammar.tsv rather than as globally applied fragments.

Bulk mandate ending (the mandate-expire.asm filename names the displayed suffix,
not an inferred timer cause):
  reference 0x1413b2a30..0x1413b2c1f
  classic   0x1413ad9a0..0x1413adb8f
  The function iterates the mandate vector and removes entries whose unit pointer
  matches the supplied unit. Count=0 returns without an announcement. Count=1
  appends "'s mandate has ended.". Count>1 appends "'s mandates have ended.".
  The branch captures only the displayed typed unit field; it never infers an
  unknown noble or translates a territory as part of a personal name.

Successful/unsuccessful result labels:
  reference 0x140b58db0..0x140b5a6b8
  classic   0x140b55df0..0x140b576f8
  "mandate was obeyed", "mandate only partially completed", "mandate ignored",
  and "nobody to punish for failed mandate" are branches of the general thought
  event label formatter. They are not fortress announcement constructor strings
  or evidence for automatic-queue failure notifications. Their complete owner is
  retained for source attribution; no fabricated announcement variant is added.

External automatic-queue announcement:
  The exact user screenshot attests this complete output production:
    Mandate Fulfilled: Automatically queued <job> x<count> for noble <unit>
  The job is typed workshop/work-order text, count is decimal digits, and noble
  is a typed unit label which may include nickname, office and territory.
  Native reference/classic EXEs and installed DFHack core/plugin DLLs do not
  contain this authored literal. Installed DFHack Lua/scripts, game save Lua,
  dfhack-config/scripts and configured additional script paths provide no source.
  The current script-paths.txt contains only comments; scripts contains README.md.

  The public author page for Sizzlin's Mandate Fulfill is a candidate producer:
    https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3735970744
  It describes a pure DFHack script which creates manager orders and emits a
  green announcement only when an order is successfully queued. It describes
  material selection, existing-order exclusion, and replacement of missing
  orders, but exposes no Lua implementation or authored branch text. The current
  local workshop payload does not contain that item. Steam's public published-
  file details API returns a manifest ID and empty file_url/filename.
  Therefore only the screenshot-attested full queue production is added. No
  invented duplicate-order, failure, material fallback, or completion notice is
  asserted to come from this unavailable script.

Runtime integration:
  data/runtime/announcement-mandate-grammar.tsv uses fortress-announcement scope.
  It is intended for the shared recursive announcement parser before permissive
  legacy catalog templates. Typed fields are $unit, $job and $digits.
  The ordinary build entry handles its import and deployment if core changes
  require a build. This source-extraction tool does not build or deploy anything.
